question: Should this explicit LiteLLM Anthropic cache-control contract require redacted live proxy proof before merge, or may maintainers intentionally accept the deterministic payload evidence alone?
rationale: The patch can prove OpenClaw’s outbound payload construction, but only a real LiteLLM route can establish forwarding, backend acceptance, cache counters, and the practical prompt-retention boundary.

options.title: Require live proxy proof
options.body: Request redacted terminal output, logs, or a reproducible transcript showing the outbound cache_control markers and Anthropic cache creation/read results.

options.title: Accept deterministic evidence
options.body: Merge based on the focused payload tests and explicitly own the remaining LiteLLM forwarding and retention-contract uncertainty.

options.title: Pause on the canonical report
options.body: Keep the linked bug as the active tracker until a maintainer or contributor can provide a real LiteLLM-to-Anthropic validation run.

recommendation.title: Require live proxy proof
recommendation.body: Request redacted terminal output, logs, or a reproducible transcript showing the outbound cache_control markers and Anthropic cache creation/read results.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent live-provider validation work makes them the strongest available routing candidate for a proof-sufficiency call.
